title: OSHA general industry walking-working surfaces practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry walking-working surfaces practice questions on 29 CFR 1910 Subpart D. Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.question: Under 1910.22(d)(2), what must happen when a hazardous condition on a walking-working surface cannot be corrected or repaired immediately?

options.A: Employees may keep using the surface for up to 7 days
options.B: The hazard is guarded to prevent employees from using the surface until it is corrected or repaired
options.C: A note in the maintenance log is enough until the next scheduled repair
options.D: Employees may use the surface once they have been told about the hazard

questions.explanation: Hazardous conditions must be corrected or repaired before the surface is used again, and "if the correction or repair cannot be made immediately, the hazard must be guarded to prevent employees from using the walking-working surface until the hazard is corrected or repaired."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.22, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Who must perform or supervise a correction or repair that involves the structural integrity of a walking-working surface?

options.A: Any employee who uses the surface
options.C: The employee who reported the hazard
options.D: A qualified person

questions.explanation: "When any correction or repair involves the structural integrity of the walking-working surface, a qualified person performs or supervises the correction or repair."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.22, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.22(a)(2), what must be maintained when wet processes are used in a workroom?

options.A: Drainage
options.B: A written spill log reviewed once a year
options.C: Standing water no deeper than 1 inch
options.D: A closed door between the workroom and other areas

questions.explanation: "When wet processes are used, drainage must be maintained" and, to the extent feasible, dry standing places such as false floors, platforms, and mats must be provided.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.22, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Outside the listed exceptions (such as elevator shafts and telecommunication towers), how far apart must ladder rungs, steps, and cleats be spaced, measured between centerlines?

options.A: Not less than 6 inches and not more than 10 inches
options.B: Not less than 14 inches and not more than 20 inches
options.C: Not less than 10 inches and not more than 14 inches
options.D: Not less than 16 inches and not more than 24 inches

questions.explanation: Ladder rungs, steps, and cleats must be spaced "not less than 10 inches (25 cm) and not more than 14 inches (36 cm) apart, as measured between the centerlines of the rungs, cleats, and steps," except in the listed cases.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.23, Ladders (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How often does 1910.23(b)(9) require ladders to be inspected for visible defects?

options.A: Once a month
options.C: Before initial use in each work shift, and more frequently as necessary
options.D: Only after a ladder has been dropped

questions.explanation: Ladders must be "inspected before initial use in each work shift, and more frequently as necessary, to identify any visible defects that could cause employee injury."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.23, Ladders (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A portable ladder is used to gain access to an upper landing surface. How far must its side rails extend above that surface?

options.A: At least 3 feet
options.C: At least 1 foot
options.D: At least 2 feet

questions.explanation: Portable ladders used to gain access to an upper landing surface must have side rails that "extend at least 3 feet (0.9 m) above the upper landing surface."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.23, Ladders (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.23(b)(10) require for a ladder with structural or other defects?

options.A: It may be used until the end of the shift and then reported
options.B: It may be used only by employees with more than one year of experience
options.C: It is repainted so the defect is covered before reuse
options.D: It is immediately tagged "Dangerous: Do Not Use" or similar and removed from service until repaired or replaced

questions.explanation: Any ladder with structural or other defects must be "immediately tagged" "Dangerous: Do Not Use" or with similar language and "removed from service until repaired in accordance with § 1910.22(d), or replaced."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.23, Ladders (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: At what angle from the horizontal must standard stairs be installed under 1910.25(c)(1)?

options.A: Between 50 and 70 degrees
options.C: Between 10 and 20 degrees
options.D: Between 70 and 90 degrees

questions.explanation: Standard stairs must be "installed at angles between 30 to 50 degrees from the horizontal." The 50 to 70 degree range belongs to ship stairs and alternating tread-type stairs.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.25, Stairways (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When may an employer use spiral, ship, or alternating tread-type stairs instead of standard stairs?

options.A: Only when the employer can demonstrate that it is not feasible to provide standard stairs
options.B: Whenever they cost less than standard stairs
options.C: Whenever fewer than 10 employees use the stairs
options.D: Whenever the employer prefers them, with no conditions

questions.explanation: "Spiral, ship, or alternating tread-type stairs are used only when the employer can demonstrate that it is not feasible to provide standard stairs."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.25, Stairways (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.28(b)(11)(ii), which flights of stairs must be equipped with stair rail systems and handrails as the rule specifies?

options.A: Only flights that rise more than 10 feet
options.B: Only flights having at least 12 risers
options.C: Only flights located outdoors
options.D: Each flight having at least 3 treads and at least 4 risers

questions.explanation: "Each flight of stairs having at least 3 treads and at least 4 risers is equipped with stair rail systems and handrails" as the paragraph sets out.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.26(d) require to keep the transport vehicle a dockboard is placed on from moving while employees are on the dockboard?

options.A: A warning sign posted on the dock door, with no other measure
options.C: Measures such as wheel chocks or sand shoes
options.D: Painting the dockboard edge a contrasting color

questions.explanation: "Measures, such as wheel chocks or sand shoes, are used to prevent the transport vehicle" on which a dockboard is placed "from moving while employees are on the dockboard."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.26, Dockboards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A dockboard is used solely for materials handling with motorized equipment, and the employees are trained under 1910.30. Guardrails or handrails are then not required if the employees are not exposed to fall hazards greater than how many feet?

options.A: 15 feet
options.C: 20 feet
options.D: 30 feet

questions.explanation: A guardrail system or handrails are not required when dockboards are used solely for materials handling with motorized equipment, "employees engaged in these operations are not exposed to fall hazards greater than 10 feet (3 m)," and they are trained under 1910.30.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.28(b)(1)(i), an employee on a walking-working surface with an unprotected side or edge must be protected from falling when that edge is how high above a lower level, except as provided elsewhere in the section?

options.A: 6 feet or more
options.C: 10 feet or more
options.D: 15 feet or more

questions.explanation: Except as provided elsewhere in the section, each employee on a walking-working surface with an unprotected side or edge "that is 4 feet (1.2 m) or more above a lower level is protected from falling" by guardrail, safety net, or personal fall protection systems.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Section 1910.28(a)(2) lists situations to which the section does not apply. Which one is on that list?

options.A: Fixed ladders that extend more than 24 feet above a lower level
options.C: Runways and similar walkways
options.D: Portable ladders

questions.explanation: 1910.28(a)(2) states that the section does not apply "to portable ladders." Fixed ladders, hoist areas, and runways each have their own fall protection paragraphs in 1910.28(b).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A fixed ladder installed on or after November 19, 2018 extends more than 24 feet above a lower level. What must it be equipped with?

options.A: A personal fall arrest system or a ladder safety system
options.B: A cage, with no personal fall arrest system or ladder safety system
options.C: A well, with no personal fall arrest system or ladder safety system
options.D: A guardrail at the top landing only

questions.explanation: "Each fixed ladder installed on and after November 19, 2018, is equipped with a personal fall arrest system or a ladder safety system." A cage or well on its own meets the rule only for fixed ladders installed before that date.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: By what date does 1910.28(b)(9)(i)(D) require all fixed ladders that extend more than 24 feet above a lower level to be equipped with a personal fall arrest system or a ladder safety system?

options.A: November 18, 2040
options.C: November 18, 2036
options.D: November 19, 2050

questions.explanation: Under the final deadline for fixed ladders that extend more than 24 feet above a lower level, "on and after November 18, 2036, all fixed ladders are equipped with a personal fall arrest system or a ladder safety system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What top edge height does 1910.29(b)(1) set for guardrail systems above the walking-working surface?

options.A: 30 inches, plus or minus 3 inches
options.C: 24 inches, plus or minus 3 inches
options.D: 42 inches, plus or minus 3 inches

questions.explanation: The top edge height of top rails "are 42 inches (107 cm), plus or minus 3 inches (8 cm), above the walking-working surface." It may exceed 45 inches if the system meets all other guardrail criteria.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.29, Fall protection systems and falling object protection—criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What force must a guardrail system withstand without failure when applied downward or outward within 2 inches of the top edge?

options.A: At least 200 pounds
options.C: At least 100 pounds
options.D: At least 150 pounds

questions.explanation: Guardrail systems must be capable of withstanding, without failure, "a force of at least 200 pounds (890 N) applied in a downward or outward direction within 2 inches (5 cm) of the top edge." The 150-pound figure applies to midrails and other intermediate members.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.29, Fall protection systems and falling object protection—criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.30(a)(2), who must train each employee on fall hazards?

options.A: Any coworker who has used the equipment
options.C: The employee, by reading the equipment label
options.D: The equipment sales representative, with no further condition

questions.explanation: "The employer must ensure that each employee is trained by a qualified person."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.30, Training requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which situation does 1910.30(c) list as one requiring retraining?

options.A: A new calendar year begins, with no change in work or equipment
options.B: The employee moves to a different shift with the same hazards and equipment
options.C: Changes in the workplace render previous training obsolete or inadequate
options.D: The employer changes its payroll provider

questions.explanation: Retraining is required when the employer has reason to believe the employee lacks the required understanding and skill, including "when changes in the workplace render previous training obsolete or inadequate."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.30, Training requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)
